reason: Both conversations correctly isolated power first, identified the snapped right-hand balance spring from the torch check and 'twang', and asked for the model number, but Conversation 1 advised replacing the springs as a pair and, once the homeowner said the unit could not be pulled out, correctly escalated to an engineer rather than improvising. Conversation 2 told the homeowner to replace only the single right-side spring and then suggested stretching a new tensioned spring into place with long-nose pliers through a tight plinth gap, which runs against the 'spring under tension' safety boundary and the sensible escalation path. Conversation 1 had minor flaws (vaguely placing springs at the 'top corners', a slightly repetitive turn and a vague final heading), but its safety handling and part advice were sounder overall.
